title: Deep learning on ECG images to prioritize testing for transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy
summary: A locally deployable AI-ECG model was developed at Yale New Haven Health (28 174 ECGs, 11 291 patients, 293 with ATTR-CM) and temporally validated. Internal AUROC was 0.84 with sensitivity 0.72 and specificity 0.86; across 5 external cohorts AUROCs ranged from 0.78 to 0.89, and in 3 screening cohorts (n = 121-645) from 0.76 to 0.91. Sequential AI-ECG then AI-enabled echocardiography raised positive predictive value from 0.24 to 0.66 and lowered sensitivity from 0.84 to 0.68. The study was retrospective and diagnostic; the authors state intended use and calibration need prospective evaluation.
ai_technology: Deep-learning AI-ECG model applied to routine ECG images or raw 12-lead signals to flag ATTR-CM
organization: Yale University; Amsterdam UMC; Amsterdam Cardiovascular Sciences

evidence.tested: Temporal and external retrospective validation against cardiac amyloid radionuclide imaging or biopsy.
evidence.unknown: Prospective benefit, calibration and intended use not tested; screening cohorts small; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Model flags patients with possible ATTR-CM from ECG images for confirmatory testing.
